verdict.rationale: Productboard's first-party MCP server lets users drive core workspace operations from their own AI agents, such as Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or Claude Code. Through those agents, users can create and update features, reschedule initiatives, move initiatives to releases and update prioritization fields. A built-in agent also handles information synthesis. However, the documented natural-language control mostly runs through an external agent client: in-product natural-language commands (Spark) are documented only for querying or acting in third-party tools like Slack and Amplitude, not for operating Productboard's own objects. Missing for 10: documented in-product natural-language command interface for operating Productboard entities, examples of natural-language prompts executing Productboard actions, and independent or hands-on corroboration that NL-driven operations work reliably.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: Now you can use any agent to add new features, reschedule an initiative, or start building off a product specification.
allowing you to employ the AI tools and agents you’re already using to access and update the product data, specifications, and documents in your Productboard workspace
Create and update features, subfeatures, initiatives, releases, objectives, key results, companies, users, feedback, documents, and more directly from your agent
Pull a spec, talk through the plan with your agent, and build.
Productboard's built-in agent handles all the information synthesis
